commands.command: Decision 0052: Workbench operator repository map and derived-graph merge/regeneration contract
commands.summary: Binds both halves of this phase: typed queries are authoritative for the operator map (never a second graph engine in the frontend), and source/config is authoritative for Git merge purposes while rog/** is derived-and-regenerable and governance/rog-capability.json is authoritative configuration a merge conflict in which is never auto-resolved.
246/246 (228 at checkpoint start, then 11 graph.search tests, 5 merge_reconcile tests, and 2 sharding-churn tests were added across this checkpoint's commits, for 246 total).

Full workspace green on Windows and, independently, on Linux-native WSL2 Debian (~/repopact-linux, synced to this checkpoint's exact pushed commits): identical counts on both platforms -- 246 repopact-graph, 21 repopact-desktop-api (17 pre-existing + 4 from the capability checkpoint), 7 generate-types drift-guard tests, 16 repopact-repository.

A new bounded, deterministic, in-memory search operation over the existing query index -- stable ID, repository-relative path, label, node role -- with a documented ranking tier (exact, exact-normalized, prefix, substring) and stable-ID tie-breaking. No repository scan, no source read, no Git, no fuzzy/embedding/LLM search; proven by a dedicated no-source-read-after-build test. Additive to query contract version 1 (unchanged). 11 new integration tests cover ranking, case-insensitivity, layer filtering, pagination/cursor rejection, and determinism. Wired through the engine protocol (graph.search) and capabilities().

graph_query(GraphQueryRequest) -> structured QueryEnvelope<...> JSON exposed through one new Tauri command (DesktopSession::graph_query already existed; only the Tauri boundary was missing). graph_status/graph_verify are read-only by construction (delegate to the identical status() call graph.verify uses; proven by graph_verify_never_mutates_capability_or_durable_graph, which asserts zero filesystem change). graph_build is the authorized rebuild control: a deliberate durable write through build_and_write, refreshing RepositoryOverview/SessionGraphState on success (proven by graph_build_enables_capability_and_refreshes_the_session) and leaving the session untouched on failure (proven by graph_build_failure_leaves_the_session_untouched, using a real .gitignore'd rog/ to force a genuine refusal).

GraphNode/GraphEdge -- explicitly disclosed as stale by the prior query checkpoint -- now carry layer/symbol_kind/location/manifest_kind/node_role and layer/derivation/location/relation_role respectively; GraphNodeKind/GraphEdgeKind gained the physical/semantic/operational variants missing from the hand-written union. Added GraphStatusView/CapabilityState/Freshness/SearchMatch/SearchRank/SearchField types and the graph.search GraphQueryRequest variant. `tsc --noEmit` and the full vitest suite (27/27: 16 pre-existing + 11 new operator-map tests) pass. A new executable drift guard (generate-types.rs's test module, 7 tests) serializes real Rust instances and asserts every JSON key is declared in the corresponding TypeScript interface, plus a GraphNodeKind variant-coverage check -- a future field/variant drift now fails this test loudly.

GraphOperatorMap.tsx: an additive 'Operator map' view inside the existing Graph tab (default remains the pre-existing ROG-010/013 relationship table, left unchanged, preserving its accepted evidence). Consumes graph_query/graph_status/graph_verify/graph_build exclusively -- no traversal/search/impact/governance logic reimplemented in React. Workflow: search (graph.search) -> select (stable node ID as selection identity) -> identity/containment (graph.context) -> bounded neighbor drill-in with layer/direction filters (graph.neighbors) -> impact/tests/governance (graph.impact/tests/governance, canonical structural_only/fixture-warning/informational-governance semantics preserved verbatim). Truncation and cursor-based load-more always visible. Freshness/capability/coverage renders as distinguishable text (never color alone), covering every ROG-039 state. Verify is read-only; Build/Rebuild requires an explicit confirmation step. A repository-generation change invalidates the selection and re-resolves it via graph.resolve rather than continuing a stale cursor. Source navigation routes work-item/decision/evidence facts into existing detail surfaces; other kinds show repository-relative path + copy-path, no new filesystem-open authority.

Prove: freshness/capability banner distinguishes enabled-but-missing from a fabricated fresh claim; search issues a real graph.search request; ambiguous/multiple results never auto-select; selecting a node loads bounded identity via graph.context; layer filters change the underlying neighbors request (not merely hide already-fetched data); truncation discloses and load-more advances via the real cursor; impact/tests/governance use their canonical operations and preserve structural_only/informational-governance text; source navigation calls the typed callback with the record's kind+id; Verify calls graph_verify only, never graph_build; Rebuild requires the confirm step before graph_build fires; essential controls (search/select/verify) work identically in compact layout with zero hover/contextmenu events fired; a changeSignal bump invalidates the selection and re-resolves it, surfacing a typed stale-selection state when the node no longer resolves.

A new, explicit, never-automatic command (repopact_graph::merge_reconcile) bounded by construction: one `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U` to enumerate unresolved paths, one scoped `git add -A -- rog/` to stage a repair -- never a per-file subprocess. Refuses closed on any unresolved authoritative source/configuration path, including governance/rog-capability.json itself. When every unresolved path is confined to rog/**, regenerates via the canonical build_and_write from the already-merged authoritative source, verifies, and only then stages -- a failed rebuild leaves the merge unresolved. A resolved explicit-disabled capability removes conflicting rog/** paths without re-enabling; a legacy-enabled repository migrates to Decision 0051's explicit-enabled declaration through the identical enable-after-proof-good path every other build uses. Wired through the engine protocol (graph.reconcile-merge) and a new `repopact graph reconcile-merge` CLI command.

commands.command: Real Git branch/merge proof (rust/crates/repopact-graph/src/merge_reconcile.rs, 5 tests using real git subprocesses)
commands.summary: (1) no_unresolved_paths_reports_nothing_to_reconcile -- a clean repo is a no-op. (2) derived_only_conflict_is_repaired_by_regeneration -- base graph committed, branch A and branch B each independently rebuild the graph on top of different source changes and commit, merging B into A leaves rog/** conflicted (confirmed via a real unresolved-path query before repair), reconcile_merge regenerates+verifies+stages it, and the repaired manifest's source_projection_fingerprint is proven byte-equal to a clean full rebuild of the same merged source -- no manual JSONL editing occurred. (3) authoritative_source_conflict_blocks_repair -- a real conflicting edit to src/main.rs on two branches blocks repair with AuthoritativeConflict{paths} naming the exact file; after the conflict is manually/responsibly resolved and committed, reconciliation proceeds (NothingToReconcile, since no graph existed on that branch). (4) capability_conflict_blocks_repair -- one branch builds+enables the graph, the other explicitly disables it via a real capability-record edit; merging produces a genuine governance/rog-capability.json conflict, and reconcile_merge refuses with CapabilityConflict, never inferring enabled-beats-disabled or its converse. (5) disabled_capability_removes_derived_conflicts_without_reenabling -- branch A and branch B both build the graph on independent source changes, branch B additionally explicitly disables (via the real disable_graph call, resolved before the merge), merging leaves only rog/** conflicted; reconciliation removes rog/ entirely and stages the removal without persisting an enabled capability, confirmed via capability::current_state == ExplicitDisabled afterward.

an_isolated_source_mutation_touches_only_a_bounded_shard_subset: a 120-work-item fixture is built (populating all 32 node+edge shards), one isolated work item is mutated, the graph is rebuilt, and the exact changed-shard set is measured: 1 of 32 shards changed; every other shard's bytes are asserted byte-identical, not merely assumed. two_independent_mutations_map_to_mostly_disjoint_shard_subsets: two further isolated mutations each touch a bounded, non-total shard subset, proving the stable hash-to-shard design does not concentrate unrelated churn onto one hot shard.

GraphOperatorMap.test.tsx's changeSignal test proves the operator map's own selection/cursor state is invalidated and re-resolved (via graph.resolve) on a repository-generation bump, never silently continuing a stale cursor or swapping in a different same-named node -- the direct UI-level consequence of Decision 0052 section 'Query/UI state after branch reconciliation'.

commands.command: Real RepoPact-scale query latency/payload evidence (engineering evidence, not ROG-032 closeout)
commands.summary: Against a disposable graph-enabled RepoPact-scale worktree (8723 nodes, 10632 edges; authoritative main never enabled), measured in-process (the actual Workbench path -- DesktopService, no subprocess per call): session open (includes initial overlay build) 1.71s; cold resolve 20.2ms/837B; search 26.5ms/30650B; orient 17.0ms/22986B; neighbors 17.4ms/42087B; impact 17.0ms/4897B; warm resolve (same session) 16.9ms; graph_status 920.5ms (dominated by the pre-existing full source-projection freshness walk, consistent with the bounded-query-orientation checkpoint's prior disclosure -- not this checkpoint's query kernel). The per-query-kernel cost stays in the tens of milliseconds even against a real ~8.7k-node graph; the UI never transfers all ~8.7k nodes to populate any operator-map view -- every measured payload here is a single bounded operation's result, not a graph dump.

Full cargo test --workspace (identical counts) on native Windows and Linux-native WSL2 Debian 13 (~/repopact-linux, never /mnt/c/...), including the real-git-subprocess merge_reconcile tests, which passed identically on both platforms. macOS: not executed and not claimed -- no macOS CI/runtime exists in this environment, and none was created to manufacture a checkbox. This is the one named residual gap keeping ROG-028 pending (see closeout).

No new mobile-incompatible code: graph_query/graph_verify/graph_build are plain Tauri commands requiring an already-open DesktopService session, exactly like every pre-existing command; on Android, session acquisition still routes through the existing typed WI060/WI061 select_repository boundary (production Android returns the existing typed 'repository.mobile-selection-unavailable' error; the debug-only app-private validation path is unchanged). No broad storage permission request was added, no content:// URI was treated as a filesystem path, no embedded Git implementation was added.
